title: Natural Language Processing Basics
overview: Cover how text is turned into numbers and how classic NLP tasks such as classification and tagging are approached.
objectives: Build bag-of-words and TF-IDF style representations

method.title: Preprocessing
method.body: Text is split into tokens and often lowercased; stopword removal and stemming are optional steps depending on the task.

method.title: Representations
method.body: Bag-of-words counts tokens, while TF-IDF down-weights words that appear in many documents.

method.title: Core tasks
method.body: Typical tasks include classification, named entity recognition, part-of-speech tagging, translation, and summarization.

method.title: Embeddings
method.body: Dense word vectors place words with similar usage near each other, replacing sparse count vectors in many systems.

pseudocode:
tokens = tokenize(lowercase(text))
vocab = build_vocab(corpus)
vector = [count(tokens, w) for w in vocab]
label = classifier.predict(vector)

playground.starterCode:
from collections import Counter
doc = 'the cat sat on the mat'
tokens = doc.lower().split()
counts = Counter(tokens)
print(counts.most_common(2))
print(len(set(tokens)), 'unique tokens')
